transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-09-28
- Start: 10:00 AM PT
- Duration: 52 min
- Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Tanya Brooks (Redwood CSM), Priya Raman (Novalex CTO), Ethan Cole (Novalex Platform), Dr. Sara Minh (Novalex ML)

Auto-summary: Quick review of sprint 2 bench results; focus on p50/p95 deltas to incumbent and routing policy recommendations. Next: dedicated slot deep bench and share security package.

[00:00] Morgan Lee: okay hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we'll keep this tight. we have about 50 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Raman: Priya here, hi.
[00:10] Ethan Cole: Ethan here.
[00:12] Dr. Sara Minh: Sara on the call.
[00:14] Diego Alvarez: Diego, Redwood SE.
[00:16] Tanya Brooks: Tanya, CSM.
[00:18] Morgan Lee: cool, thanks. agenda is: handoff of perf results we ran this week, routing/fallback recommendations, dedicated slot request and then security doc handover. Morgan to run through the numbers first.

[02:01] Morgan Lee: alright so slide one — headline: end-to-end p50 for our recommended routing is roughly 32ms lower than your incumbent at the 2048 token median profile, p95 is about 120ms lower in most runs. to caveat — those numbers vary by shard size and by KV cache warm state. when cache cold the delta shrinks.
[02:35] Speaker 1: (mumble) so p95 is, is when you said 120 that's consistent across all runs?
[02:40] Morgan Lee: not across all, it's typical when we've got warm KV cache and batching up to 8 requests. when you push concurrency up the p95 starts to widen, but our smart routing cuts over to a lower-latency variant before it hits your SLA threshold.

[04:07] Ethan Cole: can you explain the smart routing again? is that reactive only, or do you pre-route by cost tier?
[04:15] Diego Alvarez: yeah good question. so smart routing is policy driven — you can prefer latency, cost, or region. in this pilot we had policy set to latency-first with a cost cap which allowed fallback to a quantized variant if throughput demand spikes. sometimes the transcripts had 'K-V cash' reading as K-V cache, forgive the tts misread.

[05:40] Dr. Sara Minh: when you say quantized variant, are we talking 4-bit q8x or a trimmed model? we need to know quality delta for clinical notes summarization.
[05:50] Diego Alvarez: we used an int8-like path and a mixed-precision q4_x variant in the lab. qualitatively on our eval set the Rouge/LAT metrics were within 1.5 points, but for medical entity preservation we flagged a 0.7% increase in hallucinations on very edge prompts. that's in the shared eval sheet.

[07:12] Priya Raman: that hallucination stat worries me — can we threshold to keep critical paths on higher-fidelity model? like routing by prompt classification?
[07:22] Morgan Lee: absolutely, that's the recommended playbook: classify critical queries (PHI extraction, discharge summaries) to pinned high-fidelity variants and let non-critical UI text gen go to the quantized cheaper path. Diego, we annotated route rules in the repo right?
[07:32] Diego Alvarez: yes — we pushed a yaml with three routes: high-fidelity pinned, default balanced, cost-fallback quantized. we'll share that link again.

[09:05] Ethan Cole: performance numbers versus incumbent — was the baseline run on your same hardware or theirs? curious about like GPU model differences.
[09:12] Morgan Lee: good call — we reproduced the incumbent baseline using Novalex-provided test harness but on our dedicated lab nodes that match your target fleet (A100 equivalent). the incumbent numbers are their supplied public endpoint averages plus backfilled runs from your sample harness. so it's an apples-to-approx-apples but not identical to your prod region.

[11:00] Priya Raman: can we get a run using our exact k8s overlay? we want to validate KV warm/cold effects in our environment before we sign the dedicated commit.
[11:08] Morgan Lee: yes that's the next step — diego will run a dedicated-slot repro in a Novalex test VPC. Diego?
[11:15] Diego Alvarez: yep, we'll request a short-lived VPC peering or a test VPC and run the same harness. main thing we'll collect: p50/p95, GPU util, context-switching (we capture trace sampling), and KV-cache hit rates. I'll instrument more tracing so you get the tail breakdown per-step.

[13:02] Morgan Lee: quick note on throughput: for batch sizes tuned to your median payload we saw 30–40% cost reduction vs incumbent at target QPS with comparable 99th percentile bounds, though when spikey traffic hits concurrently the incumbent shows slightly better sustained throughput due to heavier autoscale settings — but our autoscaler can be tuned to match if you want predictable reserved slots.

[14:55] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) hold on — so is reserved slots the same as dedicated capacity?
[15:03] Tanya Brooks: yes reserved slots == Redwood Dedicated style, we can provision GPU pools and guarantee throughput under SLA. there are commit levels, monthly.

[16:30] Priya Raman: cost: can you show per-token vs per-request math? our finance will want a clear delta for 3m forecast.
[16:38] Morgan Lee: we'll export a per-route cost ladder — we ran one in the sheet; gist: on your expected mix, cost per 1M tokens is about 22% lower with our mixed routing, going down to 35% if you accept higher quantization on non-critical paths. we'll send the CSV.

[18:20] Ethan Cole: security questions — we need SAML + SCIM, retention logs for 13 months, and audit trails. where are we on SOC2?
[18:30] Tanya Brooks: Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we have KMS integrations and customer-managed keys on Private deployments. for Hosted we keep logs for default 90 days, enterprise add-on for 12-13 months is available. we'll attach the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide.

[20:05] Dr. Sara Minh: any PII redaction at the routing layer? we cannot have PHI go to quantized models.
[20:12] Diego Alvarez: yes that's in the route classifier; we showed a sample regex + ML classifier that pins to high-fidelity route. also you can do in-flight redaction + token-level scrub prior to hitting the inference path.

[22:45] Morgan Lee: quick demo snippet — (Morgan shares screen) here's the p95 decomposition: tokenization time, KV lookup, attention compute, and response assembly. 
[23:10] Morgan Lee: note how the KV lookup time falls dramatically after warmup on our cache; that's where the p95 gap vs incumbent shows up. if you're seeing high cold-starts in prod we can recommend TTL adjustments.

[25:50] Ethan Cole: curious — in your numbers the incumbent had a longer tokenization step. is that a tokenizer mismatch or different model tokenizer?
[26:00] Diego Alvarez: likely both — tokenizer mismatch can add 5-10ms on long inputs. we normalized tokenization in the harness but edge cases exist. we'll include tokenizer version details in the CSV.

[28:30] Priya Raman: okay let's talk acceptance criteria. For us to move forward with a pilot-to-prod conversion: p95 delta must be <= +50ms vs incumbent on critical routes and unit cost must be at least 10% lower overall. doable?
[28:45] Morgan Lee: yes — from current lab it's within that target if we implement route pinning and adjust autoscale reservations. Diego, confirm we can meet 50ms p95 delta on critical routes with dedicated slots?
[28:58] Diego Alvarez: confident — with pinned high-fidelity variants and a small reserved pool for critical queries we maintain p95 parity, we've seen sub-20ms improvement in p50 and keep p95 within 30–40ms in our dedicated runs.

[31:12] Speaker 3: (mislabel) is there any data residency issues? we want EU traffic kept in EU.
[31:20] Tanya Brooks: yes region routing is supported, and Private deployment gives you full residency. For Hosted we have region control via egress policies. We'll send the region map.

[33:05] Morgan Lee: next technical ask — Diego will run the dedicated-slot repro in your test VPC. we need a short-lived credential. Priya, can Novalex spin up that test VPC and provide sample traffic?
[33:20] Priya Raman: yes we can. I'll have Ethan share an anonymized sample by Monday.

[35:00] Diego Alvarez: I'll be instrumenting additional trace points: per-token latency, KV hit ratio, scheduler wait time. Expect a 1-hour run that we will return aggregated metrics from.

[36:42] Ethan Cole: about the fallback policy — what happens if the quantized path starts returning lower-quality text mid-session? is there an automatic rollback?
[36:52] Diego Alvarez: yes we have automatic fallback rules and a live-quality monitor. if regression crosses a threshold we can either route to the high-fidelity variant for that session or trigger a canary rollback. It's also easy to tag sessions to disallow fallback for pinned sessions.

[39:10] Dr. Sara Minh: for our eval scoring, please include entity preservation checks and hallucination rates for discharge notes. we'll need that in the sheet.
[39:20] Morgan Lee: noted — we'll expand the eval tab to include clinical-entity F1 and hallucination counts.

[41:05] Priya Raman: procurement question — what is the minimum committed capacity for Dedicated? we prefer monthly but want to start with a small commit to validate.
[41:15] Tanya Brooks: smallest committed tier is a 4-GPU pool monthly; we can also do a sprint-based dedicated slot for limited windows while you're validating. We'll include options in the pricing sheet.

[43:30] Morgan Lee: quick callouts from lab: 1) quantize fallback provides large cost wins on non-critical 2) KV cache warmup is the main lever for tail improvement 3) tokenizer normalization matters for long docs

[44:12] Ethan Cole: will you include raw traces or just aggregated metrics? we want raw sampling to profile.
[44:20] Diego Alvarez: we'll provide sampled traces plus full aggregated p50/p95 histograms; raw traces are heavy but we'll give a subset for your engineers.

[46:00] Morgan Lee: OK last section, handover: Tanya will attach SOC2 summary, SAML/SCIM guide, and logs retention options. Morgan will attach the per-route CSV. Diego will run the dedicated-slot test and return the trace pack. Priya/Ethan will provide sample traffic.

[48:10] Priya Raman: timeline — we aim to have the test VPC up by Oct 2 and initial results by Oct 6. can you make that window?
[48:18] Diego Alvarez: yes we'll aim for the 10/04 run and a short-day replay on 10/06 if needed.

[50:00] Morgan Lee: any last questions?
[50:06] Ethan Cole: none here.
[50:08] Dr. Sara Minh: no, thanks.
[50:12] Priya Raman: thanks all.

[51:40] Morgan Lee: great, wrap up: I'll email meeting notes, attach CSV + deck; Tanya will attach security docs; Diego will book the test slot and send calendar invite. thanks everyone, see you on the deep bench.
[51:52] Meeting end.
